issues.title: Archive the 21 referenced original filenames
issues.body:
The migration preserved 38 attachment references with 21 distinct filenames, but no binary originals. See sources/manifest.json and sources/README.md.

Done when:
- Export or retrieve each available original from Notion or its original location.
- Save bytes under sources/originals; record local_path, SHA-256 and status archived.
- Record any genuinely unavailable originals explicitly.
- Reconcile transcriptions against the files and retain uncertainty markers.
- Run library validation.

issues.title: Review vocabulary variants, distinct senses and 54 missing English meanings
issues.body:
The initial import groups exact normalized terms only. Four records contain differing article or auxiliary values; 54 records have no sourced English meaning. All 412 records remain needs-review.

Done when:
- Use vocabulary.csv and sources/vocabulary-occurrences.json to check variants in context.
- Review antonym pairs and near-duplicate expressions without discarding evidence.
- Separate distinct senses where needed and preserve stable IDs and source references.
- Add missing meanings with an attributed source; label added translations.
- Mark only checked records reviewed with reviewed_on.
- Regenerate views and pass checks.

issues.title: Review the 12 maintained grammar topics against course evidence
issues.body:
The grammar notes preserve existing Notion explanations and examples. Import does not establish linguistic correctness.

Done when:
- Check all 12 topics against source snapshots and available originals.
- Review scope, word order, auxiliary choices and regional usage.
- Distinguish original examples from added explanations.
- Correct canonical notes without rewriting source snapshots.
- Update review_status, reviewed_on and review notes for checked topics.
- Pass library validation.

issues.title: Open the vault in Obsidian and verify a complete sync cycle
issues.body:
Follow docs/SETUP.md on your computer. The cloud environment cannot open your local Obsidian application.

Done when:
- Clone the private repository with GitHub Desktop or Git.
- Open the clone folder as an existing Obsidian vault.
- Confirm README links, global search and Templates work.
- Create a study note, commit and push it.
- Fetch the note from GitHub to verify synchronization.
- Use Git as the vault synchronization method.

issues.title: Complete a first perfectum study session
issues.body:
Start at views/PERFECTUM-STUDY-LIST.md and grammar/the-perfect-tense-perfectum.md.

Done when:
- Create a study session note using the template.
- Choose 10 verbs and write an original sentence with each.
- Check auxiliary choices against their source contexts.
- Record mistakes, corrections, vocabulary IDs and grammar links.
- Open correction issues for uncertain course facts.
- Commit and push the study note.
